edges.title: Bernstein’s Mahler recordings, 1960–67

works.to: Bernstein’s recordings with the New York Philharmonic, 1960–67; No. 8 with the London Symphony Orchestra

edges.claim: In the 1959–60 season Bernstein led a New York Philharmonic festival for the centenary of [[mahler]]’s birth, and in 1960 he made his first commercial recording of a Mahler symphony, the Fourth. Over the next seven years he recorded all nine completed symphonies, the Eighth with the London Symphony Orchestra after a concert at the Royal Albert Hall in 1966. On 24 November 1963 he had conducted the Second Symphony in a televised memorial for President Kennedy.

edges.title: Bernstein and Ives’s Second Symphony, 1951

works.from: Symphony No. 2, written about half a century before 1951
works.to: New York Philharmonic première under Bernstein, February 1951; Columbia recording of 1958

edges.claim: The Bernstein Office dates his first performance of [[ives]]’s Second Symphony with the New York Philharmonic to 22 February 1951. The work had been written about half a century earlier and had not been played. Bernstein recorded it with the orchestra for Columbia in 1958 and again for Deutsche Grammophon in 1987.

edges.title: West Side Story after Romeo and Juliet

works.to: West Side Story, book by Arthur Laurents, opened 26 September 1957

edges.claim: Jack Gottlieb’s guide states that West Side Story is based directly on Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet. In 1949 Jerome Robbins first conceived the story as East Side Story, with a Jewish Juliet and an Italian Catholic Romeo, set in the Easter–Passover season. Arthur Laurents wrote his own dialogue and used none of Shakespeare’s words. The musical opened at the Winter Garden Theatre on 26 September 1957.

edges.title: Bernstein’s Age of Anxiety after Auden

works.from: The Age of Anxiety: A Baroque Eclogue (1947)
works.to: Symphony No. 2, The Age of Anxiety, for piano and orchestra (1949)

edges.claim: Bernstein read Auden’s The Age of Anxiety in the summer of 1947 and wrote his Second Symphony, for piano and orchestra, on its plan, using the poem’s six section titles for his movements. He said that the pianist “provides an almost autobiographical protagonist” in the search for faith. Koussevitzky conducted the first performance in Boston on 8 April 1949, with Bernstein as soloist.

sources.title: Leonard Bernstein Office: Symphony No. 2: The Age of Anxiety (1949)
